overall_reason: The 'tasteful' skin is itself the model's other default (cream paper, Fraunces with one italic word, red-orange accent, mono caps labels, 01/02 numbering, hairlines), laid over a stock SaaS skeleton with invented proof: Acme-style logo strip, '4,000+ indie teams', unsourced hero metrics and a 'Sarah Chen' testimonial.

findings.evidence: Failed T-DEFAULT-AGENT: cream #f5f1ea, Fraunces display with italic 'what' in the h1, #e34a2b accent, 33 mono tracked caps labels, '01 — Features' numbering in the nav, sections and feature rows, hairline rules and zero radius everywhere, colophon 'Set in Fraunces & IBM Plex Mono'. Two look families (warm-paper-serif 5/6, hairline-newspaper 3/4) stacked; nothing in it comes from product analytics or from this company.
findings.before: Editorial warm-paper kit applied to an analytics SaaS
findings.after: Choose the look from the product: e.g. show a real funnel or session-replay frame as the hero image and let its colours set the palette. Drop the numbering and the colophon unless the brand is a publication. [DATA NEEDED: product screenshots]
findings.why: A recognisable look family chosen without a reason is a default, whichever family it is (SLP-012, SLP-115).

findings.evidence: Failed T-FILLER: one large italic quote 'We found the exact step where users churned in a fifteen-minute session. Skittie paid for itself in one afternoon.' attributed to 'Sarah Chen — Founder, Stitchboard'. Sarah Chen is a stock generated name, Stitchboard has no link or logo, and the quote follows the polished testimonial formula (a number, a punchline).
findings.before: “…Skittie paid for itself in one afternoon.” — Sarah Chen, Founder, Stitchboard
findings.after: [DATA NEEDED: a real customer quote with permission and a link], or remove the block.
findings.why: Invented people and quotes are an integrity failure regardless of styling (INT-102, INT-104).

findings.evidence: 'TRIAL → PAID 18.4%', 'MEDIAN TIME TO VALUE 9 min', 'CHURN, 90 DAYS 2.1%' with the note '— LIVE DATA, NO QUERIES WRITTEN'. Whose data is not stated: if it is a sample dashboard it is presented as fact, if it is Skittie's own it is unsourced. The sweep caught the logo-strip count; these three were not flagged.
findings.after: Label it as an example ('Example: a 3-person SaaS, March') with a real screenshot, or remove. [DATA NEEDED: source of the figures]
findings.why: Unsourced metrics dressed as live data (INT-101, INT-106).

findings.evidence: Hero with metric panel > logo strip (Acme, Fathom, Baseline, Radar, Promptly) > three equal feature rows 01-03 > single testimonial > three pricing tiers with 'PRO — MOST POPULAR' > centred CTA band 'Stop guessing. Start knowing.' > footer. Six stock sections in stock order; restyling them as hairline rows does not change the skeleton.
findings.before: Stock SaaS order in editorial dress
findings.after: Cut the logo strip and CTA band; replace the three feature rows with one worked example (a funnel question answered end to end).
findings.why: Specific words on a default skeleton are still a default page.

findings.evidence: Failed T-RIVAL-NAME / T-FRESH-READER: 'Everything you need to grow', 'Simple pricing', 'Stop guessing. Start knowing.' fit any analytics tool (Mixpanel, PostHog, Plausible). Two are section heads and one is the closing h2.
findings.after: A line only this product can say, built from its real differentiator ('Funnels typed in English, not SQL').
findings.why: Concept capped at 5: the headings hold under a competitor's name.

findings.evidence: Failed T-OVER-CORRECTION: the removed SaaS habits (gradients, cards, icon tiles) were replaced by a new set that multiplies: 11 em dashes in 1,805 characters, a leading '—' on every kicker ('— ANALYTICS FOR FOUNDERS', '— LIVE DATA', '— NO CREDIT CARD'), 'not X' contrasts ('for founders, not data teams', 'questions, not config screens', 'No per-seat theater'), and arrows on two CTAs.
findings.before: — ANALYTICS FOR FOUNDERS, NOT DATA TEAMS
findings.after: Keep one 'not' contrast (the hero) and no leading dashes; let labels be plain words.
findings.why: The substitute habit is as recognisable as the one it replaced (SLP-113).

findings.evidence: '© 2026 Skittie Analytics — No. 014, Indie Instruments' and 'Set in Fraunces & IBM Plex Mono' are invented editorial chrome: there is no series called Indie Instruments and a SaaS footer has no reason to credit its typefaces.
findings.before: No. 014, Indie Instruments / Set in Fraunces & IBM Plex Mono

strengths: The hero sub-line has a real voice and a picturable claim: 'the clarity of a data team without the schema, the SQL, or the second mortgage.'
Pricing tiers are concrete (10k / 500k / 5M events, 7-day vs unlimited retention) and readable as a comparison.
not_investigated: eyebrows, numbered labels, Acme logo, '4,000+' and em-dash counts: reported by the sweep, not repeated
brief: no 00-contract.md, so no declared editorial brand could be checked
